Back so soon? I trust you found a way into the Darkhold? Tell me, what did you discover?
What is this talk of a primal!? Absurd!

Yes, legend says these demigods worshipped by the beast tribes feed on the aetheric energy trapped within crystals, and yes, if the Garleans [@1A(1)]were[@1A(0)] to have discovered a way to summon the creatures, it is only logical to assume that they would require an absurd amount of manifested aether─an amount found only in areas like Mor Dhona, the Thousand Maws of Toto[@1F]Rak, and the Dzemael Darkhold...
The Garleans' loathing for the beast tribes and their deities is well known. They've repeatedly attempted [@1A(1)]genocide[@1A(0)], for heaven's sake!

Yet even if this proves to be a mere falsehood conceived by the Faces of Mercy, the Admiral and her advisors must be informed. In the meantime, our investigation of the Darkhold must continue. It troubles me that this Quiliane so easily saw through a disguise that has served us for nigh on five summers, but from what I gathered from your story, she needs our help as much as we need hers. For the moment, we shall refrain from severing our ties with her organization, but we must take extra care not to reveal anything that may be used against us.
Congratulations on another assignment completed, recruit. Here are the Storm Seals you were promised.
But even if it were all true, why do it?
Greetings, friend. We are the Order of the Twin Adder─Grand Company of Gridania─and we are honored by your visit.
Perhaps you already know something of our organization─from our free literature, perhaps!? ...No? Well, please allow me to provide you with the necessary information.

The Order of the Twin Adder is an entity designed to unify and command the nation's forces. It was established by the eldest of our three Seedseers, Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna. Of course, this was done with both the consent and the blessing of the elementals.

Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna herself has left the wood and returned to the city to guide us. Under her leadership, we will overcome these outside evils that threaten the safety of Gridania and the realm at large.

We are not prepared for open war. Should it come, we will want for nearly every kind of resource. We Gridanians are not a greedy people. It is not our way to covet that which we do not have. Thus have we long refused trade with the other nations on all but the rarest of occasions.
Now more than ever, there are those who defile the forest. Why, not long ago, we received word of an Ul'dahn─a thaumaturge named Ailith─roaming the wood and laying curses upon our sacred trees.
I am told this Ailith can be found near Quarrymill. You must act quickly, before the greenwrath grows too great to appease.
A pity, that. But if you will not serve the forest, then you will not serve with us. Should your conscience get the better of you, however, you know where to find me.
I expected nothing less.

As a Seedseer, she is one with the Twelveswood, and serves it just as she serves us. But she has set aside her duty to the wood for now, that she might better focus on the threat posed by the Garlean Empire. We are now working to consolidate our nation's resources, and rally all who will answer the call.

But now, that which we want for most is manpower. Warriors, mages, crafters, gatherers─it makes no matter. All will be needed in the coming struggle. Yet starved of recruits though we are, the Order of the Twin Adder welcomes no soul who does not pay the proper respects to the Twelveswood.

Come to think... Yes... Yes, this will serve nicely as your initial duty. Seize upon this opportunity to prove your worth. Go and find this sinner, this Ailith. Find her, and expel her from the Twelveswood. If you mean to join the Order of the Twin Adder, you will see this thing done.
You must make for Quarrymill. Find the thaumaturge Ailith, and drive her from the Twelveswood for her crimes. You must act quickly, before the greenwrath grows too great to appease.

Leave the forest? Ah, on orders, are you? From the Order of the Twin Adder? Hah! There's only one Order worthy of the name in Eorzea, friend, and it is found in Arrzaneth Ossuary. These Gridanians─godsdamned mummers to a man.

These cravens live in constant fear of the elementals and their greenwrath. Do you wish to hear the truth of things? Fell a tree, and sunlight reaches the ground. The decay of the fallen trunk nourishes the soil, and there new life will sprout.
There is always good to be found in seeming evils. And so it is with me. There is purpose in what I do here. My concern is for the future of Eorzea─and it is for that future that I toil now.

I can see in your eyes that you do not believe me. But then, I doubt you were even listening. If it is proof beyond my words you require, then why not capture one of these Archons and find out for yourself?
Surely you've heard the name Urianger on your travels? He is one of the so-called Archons come to Eorzea, and travels from aetheryte to aetheryte, spouting gibberish of the Seventh Umbral Era.
He has been in these parts, burning fell glyphs into the trees. I and others like me have come to investigate the matter, and lift the curse of these glyphs. Admirable, no?
But Urianger has eluded us at every turn. We have no more information than when we came, and are no closer to knowing what significance these glyphs carry.

We have noticed a pattern in his wanderings. My companions think he will next appear to the southwest of Quarrymill. But he is a crafty one, and dangerous...so I think I shall entrust his capture to you.
You, you're an adventurer, are you not? You bear no allegiances, nor have you sworn any oaths. Tell me, then, why is it you greet me with the same hospitality as these fool forestborn?
This Archon [@1A(1)]must[@1A(0)] be taken! For the sake of all Eorzea! Once I have this Urianger, only then will I leave the forest. And happily, at that.

The Gridanians truly are a blind folk, and dumb as mummers. If the Archon Urianger is left to do as he pleases, the greenwrath of the elementals will be the least of the realm's concerns. Do they not see that?
This man is no typical foe. You will need to prepare yourself for this encounter. Be ready for anything.
Our scouts tell us that Urianger is somewhere to the southwest of Quarrymill. Find this Archon and bring him to me.
I see you have returned. But I do not see the Archon. Where is Urianger?
So the damned snake summoned a familiar this time, did he? Gods damn it all! It is impossible for us to form any kind of strategy for dealing with this elusive bastard! Still...
This other thaumaturge you speak of... It sounds as though he is well versed in the Umbral histories. And yet he is not among my own companions. I wonder...

Am I going to leave the wood? Well of course not, you bloody halfwit! You didn't do as I asked, so I won't do as you ask. That said, you [@1A(1)]did[@1A(0)] bring me some information...and in return, I will stop angering the forest.

See this letter safely to the Order of the Twin Adder. No matter what oaths I might swear, the spoken word of an outsider such as myself means nothing to them. Perhaps written and sealed, however, they will not be so quick to dismiss it.
We cannot continue on as we have all these years. A great struggle is coming, and I have a feeling the information you have brought us today may prove to be of great value.

I will not leave the forest, but I give my word that I will no longer act to anger it. That should be enough for both you and the Order of the Twin Adder, no? Go now, and take word back to your masters.
It is good to see you safely returned, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. What news of the thaumaturge? Hm? What have you brought? A sealed letter?

Indeed, everything seems in order. This document carries the proper seals, in accordance with Gridanian law. Should Ailith break her oath and sin against the wood again, we will be within our rights to deal with her as we see fit.

I thank the gods for sending you to us, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. I see now you are pure of heart. Please, come and see me again should you have any further interest in the Order of the Twin Adder.
So, you've an interest in the Order of the Twin Adder, have you? We'd be honored to welcome one such as yourself into our ranks. Aye, there is much good you could do here.
I pray you will consider serving our own Grand Company─the Order of the Twin Adder. If it interests you, I could offer you provisional enlistment as a recruit.

Should you elect to do so, you would not be required to swear any oaths, and would be free to carry out tasks for the Grand Companies of Limsa Lominsa and Ul'dah. We hear that the Maelstrom and the Immortal Flames are in sore need of adventurers as well.

Gridania has the protection of the Twelveswood, but it is we who are closest to the Garleans' domain. To put it another way, we are Eorzea's first line of defense. As such, it falls to the Order of the Twin Adder to unite the spirit and strength of the realm.

You needn't be plagued with worries of woodsin and greenwrath. The elementals have consented to all we endeavor to do, and we have the blessings of the Seedseers. I beseech you, add your strength to ours, and with us oppose the Empire! What say you?
Join the Order of the Twin Adder as a provisional recruit?
...Not your fight? It would seem you are yet ignorant as to the true scale of the Empire's ambitions─and our Order's duty to thwart them. Should you experience an epiphany, speak to me again.
Your devotion to our cause is admirable. The Order of the Twin Adder welcomes you as one of its own, and vows to do all in its power to protect and honor you as such.
As laid forth in the tomes of the first companies, deeds done in service of the Order of the Twin Adder shall be recompensed with Grand Company seals.
These seals shall be awarded whenever you see a duty through to completion in the name of our cause.
Our seal is the currency of our Grand Company, and ours alone. Though it be no coin, it can be used to purchase that which no coin can.
Gridanians have come together as one under the Order of the Twin Adder's banner. Our devotion to the Twelveswood has moved the elementals, and in turn they have bestowed upon us a bounty of gifts.
These blessed gifts bring more than just mere strength. They bring the warmth which the coming war threatens to extinguish, and the light which the coming darkness means to obscure.
But we mean to offer them only to those in possession of the Order of the Twin Adder's seals. The Grand Company seals of the other nations will not be honored here.
I hope my words have served to fan the flames of your interest. Here, allow me to present you with the first of [@1A(1)]many[@1A(0)] seals─gods willing.
It will not be long before we are able to provide you adventurers with precisely that which you seek. When the time comes, I pray you are willing to swear yourself fully to our cause.

If there is more you wish to know of the seals and their uses, speak to Serpent Sergeant First Class Haurtelle. Acquire what blessed gifts you can from her, and come to know their warmth. You'll be the better for it.
The amount of Order of the Twin Adder company seals (Serpent Seals) you have accumulated can be viewed on the Grand Companies tab under Attributes in the [@COLOR(#ff00cc22)]main menu[@COLOR($EC)].
Hello, friend. I am Serpent Sergeant First Class Sorainne Haurtelle. Allow me to congratulate you on your provisional enlistment in the Order of the Twin Adder.
I am charged with overseeing the exchange of Grand Company seals for all manner of items. Shall I explain in more detail?
We have amassed a trove of items suited to the needs of you adventurers. Unfortunately, as your enlistment is not yet official, I am only able to show you a handful of them.

Should you swear allegiance to the Order of the Twin Adder, more sought-after items will be made available to you. Of course, items are not the only things you can acquire with the seals you earn. You may alternatively use them to increase your standing within the Order.
Beyond that, there are certain other Grand Company privileges that─
What's that? You wish to know how to officially enlist in the Order of the Twin Adder? Champing at the bit, are we?
There are several ways you may achieve the honor. For example, you may come at the strong recommendation of a senior member within the company.

The simplest way, though, is to prove your worth with dedication and service. The Twin Adder takes notice of those who are capable and true of purpose. Take on whatever duties you can, and see them through to completion. Do this, and you will soon be among our ranks.

Official enlistment will be subject to certain restrictions. Each enlistee will be required to provide a quantity of Serpent Seals to demonstrate commitment to the cause. Do not worry, though, you will have ample time to acquire them. For now, why not exchange what seals you have for a nice [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,3020203,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,3020203,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)]?

Our [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,3020203,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,3020203,2,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] are indispensable concoctions. They will prove most useful while fulfilling the tasks assigned you by First Serpent Lieutenant Fulke.
Do you require an explanation?
No? <sigh> But I memorized the whole lot...
[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], you could not have arrived at a better time. Surely the elementals had a hand in this. We have a task for you─one of the utmost importance.
Elder Seedseer Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna has foreseen the coming of a grave danger─a danger which nears the Twelveswood even now.
To defend against this threat, we mean to erect an Irmin Hedge─the most powerful barrier known to the conjuring arts.
Needless to say, they are utterly defenseless in this state, and so sentries were dispatched to watch over them. Yet we have just received word that they require immediate reinforcements.

I ask that you hurry forth from the city, and head to the north and west. The linkpearl message was cut off before we could discern their precise location, but the voices were...desperate. You must help us.
You... You refuse? The task will doubtless be perilous, but...would you [@1A(1)]truly[@1A(0)] turn your back on both the elementals and the Twin Adder?
Assume the worst, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], and expect great danger. Make haste, but depart only after you have made thorough preparations. May the Twelve go with you.

It is more potent and far-reaching than the current Hedge, as it soars to the heavens above, and pierces deep below the earth. The spells used in its creation are so esoteric that only the most gifted of the conjurers may utter them, and even then only during a prolonged period of meditation.

The Irmin Hedge is more potent and far-reaching than the current Hedge. It soars to the heavens above, and pierces deep below the earth. The spells used in its creation are so esoteric that only the most gifted of the conjurers may utter them, and even then only during a prolonged period of meditation.

The trance requires that the self be set aside. It is as if they leave their own bodies. Should they be attacked in this state, or otherwise torn from their reverie, their minds will be scattered, never again to return to the waking world.

The sentries dispatched to watch over them have requested immediate reinforcements. This is no idle matter, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Head north and west of the city with all haste, and see to it that the conjurers do not come to harm!
Well done, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! Had you not drawn the attention of the imperials, our men would never have escaped with their lives.
The elementals were good to send you to us when they did. Hm? What do you have there?

You say this was sewn into the uniform of an imperial? I see... Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna made no mention of any such letter. Hmmm... I will see it delivered to the returned conjurers. Perhaps they will be able to glean something from it.

The conjurers were able to commune with the elementals living within the inks and fibers. It would seem the imperial who held this letter was not a Garlean at all, but hailed from Ala Mhigo. But why...?

Yet I am not sure our fallen Ala Mhigan's motives can be so easily explained. The contents of the letter he carried are enciphered using a code bearing no resemblance to any Garlean code we've seen. Try as we might, we've been unable to make anything of it. Stranger still, the conjurers report that the elementals within the letter sensed in its bearer a certain...nobility of spirit.

Which brings me to the matter at hand. I've another task for you, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Our only hope is that someone among the Ala Mhigans can tell us more. I would have you deliver the letter to Little Ala Mhigo in eastern Thanalan. Seek out a man there named Radulf, and learn what you can.

I am told that a great many displaced Ala Mhigans have gathered to the south of Camp Drybone─a place now called Little Ala Mhigo. I should warn you that the way is long, and that the protection of the elementals will not serve you there. Go forth with the [@1A(1)]utmost[@1A(0)] caution.

When that nation was defeated, there were countless uprisings as the citizenry sought to reclaim their freedom. But that was many years ago. Many Ala Mhigans have since grown up knowing only Garlean rule. I can only think that to them, marching under the Empire's banners comes naturally.
The elementals know all there is to know of the forest, and their whispers tell us much. But things beyond the Twelveswood are beyond their knowing.

And that is why this task has fallen to you. Travel to Little Ala Mhigo south of Camp Drybone in eastern Thanalan. See the letter delivered to a man named Radulf. He may be able to shed some light on this business.
Aye, I'm Radulf. It seems you know me, stranger, but I don't know you. What business have you here? A letter, you say?
This...this is from Hagilo! But how...? Where in the bloody hells did you get this? What's happened!? Tell me, damn you!

...No. It cannot be. Slain by a fellow enemy of the Empire? Aye, enemy, I say─for the man you killed was a member of the Resistance! Yet again, the gods make fools of us all. Damn them to the seven hells. <spit> ...But now is not the time to mourn. The Resistance must go on. The Ala Mhigans here are under my command. All have sworn to lay down their lives for Ala Mhigo's liberation.

And Hagilo was no different. He was a good man─an honorable man... Ah, but fear not, friend, I bear you no grudge. You did not know, nor could you have. Hagilo risked all to deliver this message, and you have seen it done. You deserve to hear what it says as much as I.
“Latest reports indicate Imperial Legatus Nael van Darnus has left eastern theatre. Joining forces on the western front.
“New magitek devices deployed to strongholds on western front. Have been assigned to installation labor...”[@CR]Oh, Twelve have mercy...

“Radulf... They force us to kill daily─something, anything. If only to keep us in the habit. They seek to make it a reflex in us. My grip on things is slowly slipping─on my faith...and my mind. I don't know who or what I am anymore. Darkness descends from all sides... Yet there at the center...there, brilliant, unwavering, and whole...my beacon, my lodestar...Ala Mhigo.”

...I cannot imagine what suffering Hagilo endured to obtain this information, nor do I wish to. But by bringing it to us, you've assured that he did not suffer in vain. I daresay you may even have given him peace. I have not the words to thank you.
We may hail from different lands, you and I, but we are bound by a common purpose. May fortune find us, friend.

Here, take this. It was concealed within Hagilo's report. I think it's a design for a device of some sort─perhaps those he wrote of. Perhaps someone at the Adders' Nest can make more sense of it than I.
“Changes made to invasion plans by high command. Fighting grows more fierce, imperial soldiers seem...changed. More savage, violent.
A good man gave his life to see that report and those designs out of Garlean territory. We must use them to find a way to stop the Empire. For Ala Mhigans everywhere─and for Hagilo!
The Adders' Nest welcomes you back, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. And what is this you've brought? Garlean designs...? Gods, how could the conjurers have overlooked this!?
This... Could the Empire truly be subjecting their own soldiers to such depravities?

We forestborn lead peaceful lives, guided by the wisdom of the elementals and Seedseers. But we must not forget our fellow Eorzeans in Ala Mhigo. They too have a right to live out their days in peace, and we must do all in our power to help them reclaim that right.
The will of the elementals is the will of Eorzea. The Order of the Twin Adder is of the Twelveswood, and enjoys its protection, but our charge is to bring peace and unity to all the realm.
To that end, I will see that these designs make it to the Garlond Ironworks. You have my word─we will learn whatever there is to be learned from them.

I have news, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. As you know, Elder Seedseer Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna has returned to us from the forest. She conducts her divinations tirelessly, granting us new wisdom each and every day.
By her word, it has been decided that a larger force of soldiers, this time from the Wood Wailers and Gods' Quiver both, shall brave the Thousand Maws of Toto[@1F]Rak in the South Shroud.
The Maws were closed off long ago, but recent reports suggest that someone─or something─had broken the seals and entered the accursed place. And so we sent a unit of Wood Wailers to investigate.

I am sorry to say that most never returned. From what we have since been able to gather, a legion of fiends was waiting for them in the depths─some scouters say their number was over nine thousand, but others say there is no way that could be right.

Ordinarily, I wouldn't give credence to such implausible claims, but Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna sensed the echoes of an impure voice resonating through those foul halls, calling out to beasts across the land and driving them into a blood frenzy...

Many lancers of the first expedition party were tainted with woodsin simply by virtue of being in that damned dungeon, and have since taken ill. The Thousand Maws are cursed indeed. Still, our task must be seen through to the end. Reinforcements must be sent!

Yet stretched though our resources are, I cannot in good conscience send you alone. It would be suicide. For your own safety, assemble a party of [@IF($E5(2,0),[@IF($E2(2,10),[@SWITCH(2,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(2)])],[@VALUE(2)])] to [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] members before heading to the Maws in the South Shroud. The dangers lurking within will permit no less. Will you do this?
Far be it from me to question your decision. But know that this matter is of the utmost importance to the Order of the Twin Adder.
Good. Gather what companions you will, and prepare yourselves for battle. Then travel to the Thousand Maws, north of Camp Tranquil in the South Shroud.
You will find a group of guards stationed near the dungeon's entrance. They will brief you on the situation. Go now, and may the gods go with you.
Ah, you must be [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. We've been expecting you. Aye, the Nest sent word you'd be coming to help.

But that was not all. We also received urgent orders to locate and extract a Padjal apparently at large in the Maws. To that end, an additional force of Wood Wailers has already entered, accompanied by archers of the Quiver and conjurers of the Fane.

The first Wailer expedition into the Maws was a disaster. We can't say exactly what went on down there, but the party ended up being scattered. It's a miracle any survived. Yet some did, and among them many claimed to have been saved by a Padjal who brought them water and tended their wounds.

Of course, the guards swore that no such soul had entered the dungeon, and assumed the tale to be the delirious rambling of wounded men. But the sheer number of these reports is too great to ignore. If this Padjal [@1A(1)]is[@1A(0)] real, we must do all in our power to see him safely out of the Maws.

You must also keep the following in mind─once you set foot in the Maws, I cannot permit you to re-enter until your body has had time to rid itself of the noxious residues of woodsin and aether which permeate the place.

After completing an expedition in the Thousand Maws of Toto[@1F]Rak, you will not be allowed to return immediately to the dungeon. To confirm how long you must wait before re-entering, view the Timers tab located under Attributes in the [@COLOR(#ff00cc22)]main menu[@COLOR($EC)].

As another measure to prevent the untimely loss of life to the beasts lurking below, I shall be performing a special incantation prepared by the Conjurers' Guild to draw you and your party out of the dungeon after a set amount of time has passed.
You can remain in the Thousand Maws of Toto[@1F]Rak for a maximum of [@VALUE($E8(2))] minutes (Earth time) per visit.
In addition to my spell, you may leave at any time by returning to the entrance on foot.

There are also rumors of an imperial magitek device located in the farthest reaches of the dungeon. It is said the infernal machine can instantly return a man to this spot, but I am not sure I would trust anything constructed by the Empire. Who knows what sort of havoc the contraption might play on one's humours.

Finally, if you find yourself knocked unconscious by one of the creatures, our scouts have confirmed that using a Return spell will transport you back to the dungeon's entrance, so you may continue your mission, if you so wish.
Until now, our best efforts to investigate the Maws have yielded little and less. Your help is sorely needed. I only hope this mysterious Padjal is found before it is too late.
Go now, and make what preparations you must. When you are ready, come and speak to me again.

Aid the others within, I beseech you. But do not forget the words of the Elder Seedseer. There is a vile voice sounding in those depths, driving those beasts into a murderous rage. You must remain ever vigilant.
Enter the Thousand Maws of Toto[@1F]Rak?
I understand, and you need not be ashamed of your decision. One must first conquer one's own fears before one can conquer those which trouble others.
It seems you are as ready as you will ever be. Very well. Enter now, and may the Twelve watch over you.
Why, hello there, friend. Are you injured? Lost?
No? What brings you here, then? You're looking for someone? For me?
How did I get in? Why, through the entrance, of course. But please, don't tell anyone. It would only injure the guards' pride─and my sister would be furious besides.
I sensed the moogles were in great danger, you see, and hurried here to save them. It was rash of me, I know, but there was no time to call a council, nor to appeal to the Order of the Twin Adder.
The voices of the crystals are strong here. And of late, I have heard them screaming out in terror from deep below the earth.

All living things are imbued with the power of crystals, and so their screams echo within us all. That is why so many lesser creatures are now crazed and restless. The screams have them in untold agony, driving them to madness.
The moogles are fine, incidentally.
I will leave this place together with them. But for now, I must rest. I am so...weary. I will send word to the Adders' Nest when I can. It was never my intention to trouble them.

Oh, and here─you can have this. The moogles removed it from that magitek device there. I'd take it back with me, but it...it is so...[@1A(1)]heavy[@1A(0)]. I feel it weighs me down...somehow. Take it, please. I cannot carry it a moment more.

This is a strange thing indeed. The elementals tell me that it is attempting to measure the flow of aether through the Maws─though I cannot fathom why a magitek user should deem the stuff sufficiently interesting to warrant such an invention...
You would do well to speak to the moogles, should you know their words. Mayhap there is something to be learned from all of this─some knowledge that may serve my sisters.
Kupo!
Goodness gracious me, how embarrassing! To be seen in a place such as this! Wait... You look almost exactly like an adventurer I once met, adventurer.
That's wonderful, kupo! Then I can tell you what happened! A[@1F]Ruhn saved us. I don't know what happened, but one moment we were dancing in our flower fields, and the next we were here.
I think it must have been this strange device. It's too large to move, but I levered off what parts I could. Kupooo...the mere sight of it sends shivers down my spine.
Y-you can understand me!? Are you hearing more than just incomprehensible kupo noises right now?
That's wonderful, kupo! Then I can tell you what happened! A[@1F]Ruhn saved us. I don't know what happened, but one moment we were dancing in our flower fields, and the next we were here.
I think it must have been this strange device. It's too large to move, but I levered off what parts I could. Kupooo...the mere sight of it sends shivers down my spine.

A job well done, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Word arrived from the Adders' Nest. It seems you found our Padjal within the Maws. To think it was none other than Seedseer A[@1F]Ruhn[@1F]Senna! I should add that he and the moogles have since departed.
It's a relief to know he's no longer in harm's way. This mission has been a success, thanks to you.
The forces deployed to find him have returned to Gridania, as well. First Serpent Lieutenant Fulke spoke of a strange magitek device within the Maws.
You saw it, too? The conjurers within warned the others not to go near it. They said it gave off a vile, foreboding air.

This [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000260,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000260,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] is from the device!? You must take it to the Adders' Nest at once! I daresay First Serpent Lieutenant Fulke will be eager to have it properly examined.
Yet another job well done, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].

No doubt you realize by now, but the Padjal you found was none other than Seedseer A[@1F]Ruhn[@1F]Senna, youngest of the three siblings, and brother to Kan[@1F]E and Raya[@1F]O. Gridania is the better for having him back. It was a great thing you did, braving the Maws and convincing him to return.
Elder Seedseer Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna herself has been informed of your exploits. I can also report that we have made progress in our investigation of the woodsin permeating the Thousand Maws.

The device installed there is of Garlean making. And so the question that concerns us most now is this─how did imperials manage to infiltrate the Twelveswood [@1A(1)]and[@1A(0)] the Maws with such an unwieldy contraption? And all while the elementals looked on! A troubling thought indeed...

Our uncertainty only grew when we were informed of the conjurers' findings. By attuning to the forces within the Maws, they discerned that the device's purpose was to measure the flow of aether in the area. But why should the Empire, with all their infernal technologies, take an interest in that?
If only we could take it─or just a piece of it─to the Garlond Ironworks. Surely the engineers there would be able to glean something useful from it.
You have a piece of the device!? Where did you get it?

From the hands of a moogle to Seedseer A[@1F]Ruhn[@1F]Senna, thence to you, from you to the Order of the Twin Adder, and from us to the Garlond Ironworks! Well, this is no mere coincidence. I do believe our fortunes in this war are changing!
Your deeds continue to astound, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. The Order of the Twin Adder thanks you. Here is your reward.
The trees of the Twelveswood are restless, and so too the hearts of men. An ill wind blows across Eorzea, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], unsettling all it touches. Surely you feel it as well.

The Garleans grow bolder by the day. Their soldiers are turning up in nearly every corner of the realm, and ever more frequently. Even more distressing, we've recently learned that control of Dzemael Darkhold in Ishgard has fallen into imperial hands.

Perhaps now you realize the urgency of our situation. Gridania's northern border is at our enemy's mercy. Something must be done. Elder Seedseer Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna has ordered that able men and women be sent to aid Ishgard on behalf of the Order of the Twin Adder.
Yet there is one remaining matter that worries us...

The Darkhold is a military fortress, and lies not far from the walls of Ishgard itself. Its construction was left incomplete, yes, but even so, the knights of the north would have given their lives to defend it. The Garleans could not have gained entry easily.

Yet gain entry they did, and the knights were slow to counter. Now the imperials are entrenched, and the resources of Ishgard are stretched thin in the effort to oust them from the Darkhold. There must be some sort of explanation for all of this.
It seems Gridania has need of you yet again, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. We must send one of our own to observe the knights closely. Only then may we hope to learn what it is they mean to do.
If you would play your part, make for Owl's Nest in the eastern lowlands of Coerthas. Once there, seek audience with Ser Yuhelmeric, lord commander of knights of House Durendaire.
...I had hoped the obvious urgency of our plight would move you to assist us. Apparently not.
Excellent. But I must warn you─the Darkhold is rife with dangers. Stint not in your preparations.
We are gathering what souls we can to answer Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna's call and march north to fight alongside the Ishgardians and retake the Darkhold.

He will grant you entry into the hold─provided you are well accompanied. You will be required to form a party of [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] to [@IF($E5(8,0),[@IF($E2(8,10),[@SWITCH(8,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(8)])],[@VALUE(8)])] brave souls. Can you do this, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]?
Head to Owl's Nest in the eastern lowlands of Coerthas. There find a Ser Yuhelmeric, lord of the knights of House Durendaire. He will likely grant you entry to the Darkhold.

The Darkhold is rife with dangers. Stint not in your preparations. You will require of party of [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] to [@IF($E5(8,0),[@IF($E2(8,10),[@SWITCH(8,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(8)])],[@VALUE(8)])] brave souls to gain entry.

To enter the Dzemael Darkhold, you must be in a party consisting of between [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] to [@IF($E5(8,0),[@IF($E2(8,10),[@SWITCH(8,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(8)])],[@VALUE(8)])] Disciples of War or Magic with a level of [@VALUE($E8(4))] or higher.
Well met, friend. The Order of the Twin Adder sent word that you would be coming.

We were gratified to learn of Kan[@1F]E[@1F]Senna's promise of reinforcements, but...I must confess, I had not expected them to consist of mercenary adventurers. I take from this that the might of Gridania is dedicated solely to the protection of her own borders.
You have traveled far, and so I shall not do you the disservice of bandying words.

The enemy has not been idle. They command vast legions, and do so masterfully. Reports from the other nations echo our own, with claims of Garlean operatives in nigh on every city, hamlet, and camp in the realm─operatives disguised as adventurers, that their comings and goings might avoid suspicion.

We have seized countless of these brigands attempting to steal their way into the Darkhold ever since the discovery of the crystal veins within. And now here [@1A(1)]you[@1A(0)] are, the latest fearless adventurer, sent to aid in the heroic reclamation...

You will forgive me, but recent days have bred in me a certain...skepticism. The banner of the Twin Adder lends weight to your claim, but you must still prove yourself both loyal and able. I shall permit you entry into the Darkhold─but require that you slay the Garleans we know to be holding the captain's quarters. Your word is your bond, no doubt, but I shall require [@1A(1)]material[@1A(0)] proof of their demise, nonetheless.
The place you seek will not be reached easily. The foul beasts within will see to that. Yet if you are blessed with ability, and true of purpose, then mayhap the gods will see fit to deliver you.

Also, I will not allow you to attempt this task alone. You may enter as one of a party of [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] to [@IF($E5(8,0),[@IF($E2(8,10),[@SWITCH(8,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(8)])],[@VALUE(8)])] members, or not at all. Your companions may be of your own choosing.

Speak to the guards stationed before the entrance should you wish to know more. I trust you know where the Darkhold... Ahem. I gather from your vacant expression that you did [@1A(1)]not[@1A(0)] know that the Darkhold lies in the central highlands of Coerthas. <sigh> Just go, and gods help us all...

To enter the Dzemael Darkhold, you must be in a party consisting of between [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] to [@IF($E5(8,0),[@IF($E2(8,10),[@SWITCH(8,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(8)])],[@VALUE(8)])] Disciples of War or Magic with a level of [@VALUE($E8(4))] or higher.

The Black Shroud is ill at ease. You can feel it even from here. I cannot help but wonder if the elementals are hiding something from the forestborn─deceiving them somehow. Of course, such a thought would never cross the mind of a Gridanian.

Business with Ser Yuhelmeric, you say? So the forestborn send a mercenary adventurer to trade words with the lord commander of House Durendaire's knights? <spit> I see those tree-loving arseholes [@1A(1)]still[@1A(0)] haven't learned their bloody courtesies.
The Grand Company of Gridania, risen again. I pray your Order of the Twin Adder proves a powerful ally in the coming struggle.

Count Dzemael himself oversaw the Darkhold's continuing construction. It was to be a great bastion in our war against the dragons. But then the accident happened...and the abominations came. We dare not send men to labor there now, and so it stands incomplete.

I have my doubts as to whether it [@1A(1)]was[@1A(0)] an accident, of course. I make it the work of heretics─sent by the dragons to disrupt the building effort, lest we secure a surer foothold in the highlands.
Take care not to tire within the hold, nor spend all your strength. The ghastly beasts within are large enough as it is. We can ill afford to offer them a free meal! Hahaha!
You represent the Order of the Twin Adder, do you not? I suspected you might. House Durendaire sent word of your coming.
If you truly value your life, then listen carefully to my words.

The depths of the Darkhold are said to contain a rift through which the creatures of the void gain entrance to this realm. And they are not all that passes through. Foul miasmas seep into the caverns, clogging the lungs and poisoning the minds of any who linger too long.

After completing an expedition in the Dzemael Darkhold, you will not be permitted to return to the area immediately. To confirm how long you must wait before re-entering, view the Timers tab located under Attributes in the [@COLOR(#ff00cc22)][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)]main menu[@COLOR($EC)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)].

To ensure that the noisome mists are not allowed the opportunity to tighten their grip, I shall be casting a spell upon you that will teleport you back here to my side after the passing of several bells.
You can remain in the Dzemael Darkhold for a maximum of [@VALUE($E8(2))] minutes (Earth time) per visit.
You are free to leave the Darkhold on foot at any time, of course─assuming you remember the way.

Otherwise, it is said there is a magitek device in the farthest reaches of the hold with the power to return a man to this spot in the blink of an eye. I wouldn't go trusting [@1A(1)]that[@1A(0)] with my worldly being, though.

Oh, and should you come to grief down there, others before you have confirmed that using a Return spell will transport you back to the Darkhold's entrance, so you may continue your mission, if you so wish.
And that is all the information I can give you. If I may offer an opinion, though─this is an evil place, forsaken by the Twelve and embraced by devils. Leave while you still can, and don't look back.
But seeing as you will not, the least I can do is offer you one last opportunity to make your final preparations. Speak to me once more when you are ready.
All items in a player's loot list will automatically be transferred to that player's inventory upon leaving the dungeon. Items unable to be obtained will be lost.
Enter Dzemael Darkhold?
I see you could not be swayed. Very well.
I had best not discover this was all an elaborate jape at my expense or Twelve help me I will denounce you as a heretic and see you drawn and quartered!
The deed is done? Perhaps I underestimated you, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Please, take word of this to Ser Yuhelmeric at Owl's Nest.
I demanded that you prove yourself loyal and able. Let us see if you have. What evidence do you bring me of the Garleans you claim to have slain within the Darkhold?
This... One of the Garleans was carrying [@1A(1)]this[@1A(1)]? Are you [@1A(1)]sure[@1A(0)]!? Speak false and I shall have your tongue!
Forgive me. I spoke out of passion. That was not...knightly. Seeing this relic, I...I forgot myself.

The [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,11000264,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,3,11000264,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)] is the mark of a heretic. The mark of one who has given his soul over to the dragons. Doubt not that they are cunning creatures, beguiling to the weak of mind, and all who lust after power. Such men are apt prey for the foul spells of the dragonkin. Their wills are broken, and with them their oaths to Ishgard. For that, we brand them heretics.

It shames me to speak it, but the imperial soldier who carried this may once have been one of our own. Perhaps he turned cloak and fled to the Empire. Perhaps they founded their siege strategy upon his intelligence. Perhaps he guided these bloody Garleans across our borders and into the Darkhold...

...But it profits us naught to speculate. We have yet to discover what path the Garleans marched into Coerthas. Without that knowledge, we cannot devise a strategy to counter their movements and reclaim the Darkhold. Nevertheless, the information you provided [@1A(1)]has[@1A(0)] served to clarify matters.
You have done all you can for now, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], and for that I am grateful. Return to Gridania, and report to your masters at the Adders' Nest.

The lives of such craven traitors are forfeit. All know that the knighthood will hunt them to the ends of the realm, and so, to escape the See's justice, some turn to the Empire, divulging the Darkhold's secrets to curry favor with their new lords.
Come, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], I have been awaiting your return. Tell me of your exploits in the north.
Gods, to think the Garleans have forced their way so deep into the Darkhold... This is distressing news indeed.
And Ser Yuhelmeric claimed there was a heretic among the imperials? And possibly a former knight of Ishgard, no less?

Then these so-called isolated incidents in the north are isolated no more. Here, too, we have heard reports of men and women from across the realm defecting to the Empire. But I had imagined them brigands or bandits─not anointed knights entrusted with the secrets of Ishgard!
Ser Yuhelmeric wishes to extend his gratitude once again on behalf of Ishgard. In addition, it seems your distinguished service has earned you the right to enter Dzemael Darkhold as you please.

Ishgard and our own Gridania share a history of animosity. We were once at war, long ago, each nation seeking the annihilation of the other. Yet now we must join forces against a common enemy, lest we share the fate of Ala Mhigo.
But I digress. You have done well to serve in the face of such difficulties, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. The Order of the Twin Adder is truly grateful.
Long now have the wheels of the Garlean war machine been in motion. Yet perhaps those wheels are far grander in scale than any among us had imagined.
This is the home of the Immortal Flames, friend. We are the Grand Company of Ul'dah, and we welcome you to our halls.
You adventurers have proven as useful as any in gathering intelligence. We have need of a good [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)] such as yourself.
The Immortal Flames are dedicated to safeguarding the peace and prosperity of Ul'dah against the growing menace that threatens our realm.

Flame General Raubahn Aldynn of the Syndicate is our founder and commander. Under his leadership, we strive to unite Ul'dah's martial and mercantile strengths, and bring them to bear on our common adversities.

Yet more often than not, we lack the numbers to fulfill so grand an aim, and true talent is a rarity indeed. I beseech you to lend us your strength. Add your name to the Immortal Flames' roll of heroes.

There is a certain merchant within the city─a man of great wealth and influence. Blinded by both avarice and arrogance, he continues to refuse our appeals for aid. No doubt he has naught but disdain for the Syndicate and the Immortal Flames, but he [@1A(1)]must[@1A(0)] be rallied to our cause. I would like you to try and convince him of this.
You would let such an opportunity simply pass you by? As you wish. But should you reconsider, the offer stands.
Without the support of men of influence like Taylor, the Immortal Flames' cause is as good as lost. Do whatever you must to convince him, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].

The merchant's name is Taylor. He can be found at the docks where the ferries from Limsa Lominsa put in. Persuade him to assist us, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], and the Immortal Flames may well greet you as a [@IF($E9(4),sister,brother)] when next you come.
He can be found at the docks where the ferries from Limsa Lominsa put in. Win us his trust and allegiance─and most importantly, his gil!
Without men of influence like Taylor, the Immortal Flames' cause is as good as lost. Do whatever it takes to win his support, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].
What's this, then? From the looks of it, I'd say the Immortal Flames have sent me another of their lapdogs. Come to try and talk me out of my money, have you?
Come now, do you truly expect me to believe that an organization thrown together in so hasty and desperate a manner can truly protect me and my interests?

Hah! Those hopeful heroes certainly have a thing or two to learn about doing business. Trust, faith, sincerity, mutual benefit─these are the pillars of all successful dealings. The Flames must show me what they have to offer before they see a single gil from my coffers.
Unless... If the Flames were to win the support of a man known as Urianger, I might be more inclined to consider entering into an agreement.
He is one of these mysterious souls traveling from aetheryte to aetheryte, preaching dark words of the coming of the Seventh Umbral Era.

I'll not be fooled by these so-called Archons, and neither should you. Urianger's words are all he has, and that's all they are─words. This Seventh Umbral Era is either a hoax or a trick of the old fool's mind. Be that as it may, fear is spreading among the smallfolk like wildfire. But in the billows of smoke, I smell opportunity!
If what I've heard is true, you're most likely to find Urianger near these very docks. Head just southeast of here and odds are you'll come upon him before long.
If I'm going to turn this hunch into profit, though, I'll first need information! I must know precisely what is transpiring. So go and find this Urianger, and bring him to me─by force, if you must.

Haha, you would do well to learn the value of perspective, my friend. Where others see danger, I see potential! To them, fear, to me, fortune! I smell an opportunity here, but I need to know the details before I can act.
Time is money. Go now, just to the south and east of here. You're like to find this Archon named Urianger at these very docks.
Well, look who it is. I confess I was just asking myself whether you would return. Have you found our good Urianger, then?
Escaped...? Gods, this bastard is more elusive than a greased opo[@1F]opo. I thought an adventurer perhaps capable of the task, but it seems I was wrong.

Bah, there is no use nor gil in lamenting over such failures. You were able to procure some new information, so your efforts were not entirely lost. This Hyur bloke you spoke of seems to know quite a bit about the Umbral Eras.

The question I now find myself asking is whether all of this was mere coincidence. Hmmm...I think perhaps that I should inform my superiors. I am not one to ignore my instincts─it is they that have made me a rich man, after all.

You failed to fulfill the task I set before you, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Still, you are not wholly undeserving of some praise for your show of sincerity and diligence. Allow me to give you a second chance.
I am willing to fund the Immortal Flames... But I shall give to them only so much coin as they give power to me. You may tell that barbarian Raubahn those are my terms.

I am willing to fund the Immortal Flames... But I shall give to them only so much coin as they give power to me. Now run along to the headquarters of the Flames, and tell that barbarian Raubahn those are my terms.
Welcome back, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]. Tell me, how did you fare? You carry a letter from Taylor? Show me...

So, he demands power to command the Flames in exchange for his gil... I suppose we should have expected as much. I will see to it word reaches Flame General Raubahn─both of this and of your loyal service.
As for enlistment in the Immortal Flames, it is I who have been entrusted to make final decisions regarding recruits. Come and speak to me again if you are still interested. That is all.

What preparations there were are now complete, and the Immortal Flames have been rekindled. Even now, we are carrying out operations across the region. I would like to offer you the chance to join the Immortal Flames as a recruit, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)].

We cannot offer you official enlistment as of yet, but I have seen what you are capable of, and concede that it would be remiss of me simply to turn you away. The position is a temporary one, and not binding. It will not preclude you from assisting the Grand Companies of other nations.
Yes, as you are by now no doubt aware, the Order of the Twin Adder of Gridania and the Maelstrom of Limsa Lominsa have been remade as well.
But ours is the richer nation. The wealth of Ul'dah will see to it that we of the Immortal Flames have the best weapons and armor in our armories, and the most abundant resources at our disposal.
So which will it be? Will you join us and oppose the Garleans in the name of freedom? Or will you cower as other brave souls step forward to fight this war for you?
Join the Immortal Flames as a provisional recruit?
So be it, but our doors shall remain open. You know where to find us should you [@IF($E9(4),have a change of heart,locate your manhood)].
A wise and noble decision. I have no doubt that you will achieve greatness marching under our banners.
And now, duty requires that I speak to you of our Grand Company seals.
As an enlistee, you will be given certain tasks. Upon completion of these tasks, your efforts will be rewarded with a payment of Grand Company seals.
These seals are the currency of the Immortal Flames. They are not coin, but they will enable you to purchase goods from us all the same─goods that cannot be obtained otherwise.

Our stores contain items made by the finest artisans and craftsmen in Ul'dah. But they are available only to those deemed worthy of the Immortal Flames, and only then through the exchange of seals earned through faithful service.
You are no stranger to the ways of this nation. With enough gil, one can buy power, fame, love. Just so with our seals. They can be used to purchase more than mere items.
But know that only our own Flame Seals are accepted here. Those of the Grand Companies of Limsa Lominsa and Gridania will not be honored.
What's that you say? You'd like to get your hands on some of these seals? Hahaha!

Well...I suppose I could stand to part with a few, given your obvious enthusiasm. After all, I'm [@1A(1)]sure[@1A(0)] you will be joining our Immortal Flames at the first opporunity. Isn't that right?
Now, do you see that lovely Miqo'te standing just next to me? That is Flame Sergeant First Class Rahz, and she knows all there is to know of seals. Speak to her if you wish to learn more.

The amount of Immortal Flames company seals (Flame Seals) you have accumulated can be viewed on the Grand Companies tab under Attributes in the [@COLOR(#ff00cc22)][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)]main menu[@COLOR($EC)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)].
I am Flame Sergeant First Class U'sanzi Rahz. Allow me to congratulate you on your provisional enlistment in the Immortal Flames.
I am responsible for the issue of gear and items, but only to those in possession of Flame Seals─the currency of our company. You are new to us. Tell me, do you require any further explanation?

The Immortal Flames have established this store so that its members might use their Grand Company seals to purchase various gear and items. We have taken special care to amass those articles we feel will be most appreciated by you adventurers. The items available to you as a provisional recruit are limited, however.
When the time comes for you to pledge yourself fully to the Immortal Flames, and win great victories under her banners, you will find ever more impressive gear available to you.
But that is not all. Your Flame Seals can also be used to raise you through the ranks of our organization. There are other privileges beyond this, as well.
But entry into our ranks does not come easily─it must be earned. If you have undertaken any tasks at the behest of First Flame Lieutenant Aubrey, then you know of what I speak.

We wish to bring only the most dedicated and loyal of adventurers into the Immortal Flames. Our Grand Company is a symbol of Eorzean freedom. We put these duties to recruits to weed out the weak and the unworthy.
Only after you succeed in carrying out the tasks put to you, and are deemed worthy of the honor, will you be welcomed as one of our own─as one of the Immortal Flames.

I should also mention that officially enlisting in the Immortal Flames will cost a certain amount of company seals. But worry about crossing that bridge when you come to it. For now, I urge you to exchange what seals you have here for [@SWITCH([@SHEET(itemData,3020204,41)],[@COLOR(#fff3f3f3)],[@COLOR(#ffc0ffa0)],[@COLOR(#ff60c8ff)],[@COLOR(#ffb38cff)],[@COLOR(#ffffa666)],[@COLOR(#ffe5dd7e)])][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)][@SHEETEN(xtx/itemName,1,3020204,1,1)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)][@COLOR($EC)].
They will prove most useful while fulfilling the tasks put to you by First Flame Lieutenant Aubrey.
Inquire further?
So new to our ranks and yet already so familiar with our ways? Somehow I doubt it.
You have come to aid the cause? That is good. I have an urgent task for which I require a [@IF($E9(4),woman,man)] of your proven loyalty.
A unit carrying arms and munitions from near Ala Mhigo has come under attack. It would appear that the Garleans have blockaded the trade route.
That route is Ul'dah's lifeline to the East, and carries the bulk of our trade. If we lose it, it will cost the nation billions, and effectively neuter our military.
Should it come to that, we would lack the strength to withstand a direct attack. We must break the Garlean blockade. We [@1A(1)]must[@1A(0)]!

We have learned what we can of the imperials holding the road. They are known as the Hellhounds. According to our intelligence, they have taken up a position close to the Golden Bazaar. You must depart as soon as you are able.
I...understand. This is not a task to be taken lightly. The Hellhounds are notorious for their savagery. It is said even among the Garleans they are known as the Empire's “mad dogs.”
Then return to us only after you have seen the thing done. The Immortal Flames will not accept failure.
The route blockaded by the Empire's Hellhounds is Ul'dah's lifeline to the East. It was established by Lord Lolorito, and has brought great profit and prosperity to our nation.

Surely you know of Lord Lolorito. No individual is more influential in Ul'dah's trade than he. Not only is he head of the East Aldenard Trading Company, but he holds a seat on the Syndicate as well. He is one of the richest and most powerful men in all the realm.

The clothing and accessories handled by the East Aldenard Trading Company enjoy popularity throughout the realm. Lord Lolorito has invested a great deal in the development of the eastern route, and has a say in all the goods that move along it.
I have received word of your deeds from our scouts in the field. You have done exceptionally well.
The lawless fiends ran rampant under the protection of the imperial banner, pillaging and plundering. It was only when Lord Lolorito bribed the scoundrels that the safety of the road was restored.
Unfortunately, that provided the Empire with an excuse to march on east Thanalan, ostensibly to put down their rogue Hellhounds.

If that happens, we will be forced to rely almost exclusively on sea routes through Limsa Lominsa. Yet the Empire is making its presence felt there as well, and the situation grows more unstable by the day.

It won't be long before the Garleans impose a sea blockade─assuming the threat of war doesn't force the Lominsans to close their ports first. It makes little difference, of course─either one would mean an end to shipping.

There is no more time to explain. Head west to the ferry docks and seek passage to Limsa Lominsa. There you are to secure us a contract with no fewer than [@IF($E5(3,0),[@IF($E2(3,10),[@SWITCH(3,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(3)])],[@VALUE(3)])] famous arms dealers.
These Hellhounds may march under the Empire's banner, but they are in truth no more than honorless sellswords, hired to harry our borders.
Naught but lies and posturing, of course, but we will likely be forced to abandon the route all the same.
Yet ours is a mercantile nation. Without trade, we are nothing. We must reclaim the eastern trade route, before all hope is lost. And to that end, we must equip ourselves.

If worst comes to pass, the Garleans will attempt to blockade trade routes over both land and sea. Needless to say, we cannot allow that to happen─yet we lack the weapons to prevent it. I need you to travel to Limsa Lominsa, and secure for us arms contracts with [@IF($E5(3,0),[@IF($E2(3,10),[@SWITCH(3,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(3)])],[@VALUE(3)])] dealers.
So, come to Woolvale Arms lookin' for a contract, have ye?

Them Garleans've cast their net o'er all Eorzea, and every day sees it drawn tighter about us. Most folk here reckon they mean to raze the whole bloody realm to the ground. Hells, merchants from across the seas have already put an end to their dealin's here.
But there ain't no business like war, and no business partner like Lord Lolorito. If it be arms ye're after, Woolvale'll be happy to oblige ye.
Who ye representin'? The East Aldenard Tradin' Comp'ny? Hah! That Lolorito don't wait around, does he!? S'pose that's to be expected, though, seein' as how he's got more gil than the gods.

Gridania's right on the Empire's doorstep, and Lominsan regulations are too bloody strict by half, so Woolvale's more than pleased to enter into terms with the honest folks o'er at the East Aldenard Tradin' Comp'ny.
The East Aldenard Trading Company seeks to deal in arms with us? Teeheehee!

Still, Lord Lolorito's successes speak for themselves, as does his influence. The man genuinely has a gift for the merchant's trade. Speaking of which, is it [@1A(1)]true[@1A(0)] what the smallfolk say? Does Lord Lolorito [@1A(1)]really[@1A(0)]...

...shit gil? Teeheehee! I jest, of course! Gods, please don't tell him I said that! Of course we will enter into a contract with the good lord! Straight Edge Traders would be [@1A(1)]honored[@1A(0)] to do business with the East Aldenard Trading Company.
But of course it does. Lord Lolorito is the proprietor of the Eshtaime and Sunsilk names, and still others besides. Purveyors of such opulent goods are always first to feel the pinch in times of war.
If it is arms Lord Lolorito seeks, Straight Edge Traders will be happy to deliver. You have our word. Teeheehee!
We are always honored to welcome an emissarrry from the East Aldenard Trading Company. All know that dealings with Lord Lolorito have never yet failed to yield a profit!
He will have the contract he seeks. The Gigas Forge is at your serrrvice.
We have been praying for the day an opportunity such as this would come along. The Gigas Forge is at your serrrvice!
You were able to secure all of the contracts? Well done, [@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! I see your bravery is matched by your powers of persuasion!
I have some good news, as well. We were able to agree to terms with the Garleans. The trade route to the East has been named a demilitarized zone. Shipping will continue safely, for now.
It should come as no surprise to hear it, but Lord Lolorito was not sitting idly by while the road was being lost. I shudder to think what sums exchanged hands to secure this superficial peace...

But there is no need to worry. Whatever money was lost will soon be made back tenfold. While the other nations have already begun to limit their trade, Ul'dah has seized near complete control of the flow of arms─and this upon the eve of war!
And so you see what it is that makes Ul'dah great─the ability to find fortune in every misfortune.

The Garlond Ironworks is producing the finest weaponry in the realm, and we mean to make them the most sought-after goods on the market! Being a member of the Immortal Flames, these weapons will of course be at your own disposal as well, should you rise high enough in our ranks.
[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)]! Thank the gods, what a timely coincidence. There is a favor I would ask of you.

In Gridania's South Shroud lies a dungeon known as the Thousand Maws of Toto[@1F]Rak. It is a gaol, once used to hold those who sinned against the wood, they say, but it was sealed off long ago. Of late, however, there have been numerous reports of all manner of beasts and fiends gathering and lurking within.
As to why they should suddenly be drawn to the place, I cannot say─and so I sent a man to Gridania to find out. Sadly, however, his efforts to gather intelligence proved fruitless.
Still, these events in the forest cannot be ignored. It may well be the Gridanians are hiding something from us─which is why we dispatched a small contingent to the Thousand Maws to investigate.
But those I sent encountered more hardship than anticipated. Their search proved more and more perilous by the day until, a short time ago, all contact was lost.

[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], we ask that you travel to the South Shroud, and learn what has become of our men. But you must first obtain leave at the Wailing Barracks to do so. I will not lie to you─the danger is great. Consider well before you answer.

You are a brave soul, indeed. Go then, and make first for the Wailing Barracks. Your mission will take you into the Gridanians' domain, so you will need their permission if you are to search for our missing men.
I understand your apprehensions. Should you reconsider, you know where to find me.

Though their call was heeded and the Eorzean Alliance formed, the Gridanians remain as wary and suspecting as ever. As a sign of good faith, Ul'dah has sent a unit to aid in surveying the Thousand Maws of Toto[@1F]Rak.

[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], we ask that you travel to the South Shroud, and learn what has become of our men. But you must first obtain leave at the Wailing Barracks to do so. I will not lie to you─the danger is great. Consider well before you answer.
Make first for the Wailing Barracks. You will be in the Gridanians' domain, so you will require their permission if you are to search for our missing men.
Missing Ul'dahns? Aye, I remember them. I'm not bloody like to forget.

Looked like the Immortal Flames scraped the bottom of the adventurer barrel when they put that lot together. Those damned fools are on their own, they are. Ignored every word I offered by way of warning and went on unescorted.

These are restless times. We Wailers have our hands full with patrols and countless other duties. We'll not waste what little resources we have chasing after fools from Ul'dah that go diving headfirst into whatever dungeon tickles their fancy.

If you're hells-bent on chasing after them, I'll not stop you. But neither will I give you leave to enter the Maws alone. I'll notify the guards posted at the dungeon entrance of your coming. Oh, but before going in yourself, it might be worth asking them if your idiot friends ever even made it that far.

Only parties consisting of between [@IF($E5(2,0),[@IF($E2(2,10),[@SWITCH(2,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(2)])],[@VALUE(2)])] and [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] Disciples of War or Magic with a level of [@VALUE($E8(4))] or above will be granted entry to the Thousand Maws of Toto[@1F]Rak.

Told them those halls were named forsaken by the Seedseers, and sealed for it. But they hadn't a mind to listen. Kept cursing and shouting and demanding they be let into the Thousand Maws. Was all we could do to chase them out of here before things took a turn for the worse.
That lot? Don't get me wrong, we are grateful to Ul'dah for their aid, but...

That lot didn't have much of a mind for cooperating. We asked that they wait a spell before heading into the Thousand Maws. One does not simply go storming into a place thought so tainted with evil as to be sealed by the conjurers.
They made themselves scarce after that, and then disappeared altogehter. If I were to venture a guess, I'd say they'd gone off and into the Maws of their own accord, the bloody fools.

We haven't the men to spare to conduct a search. Would you see to it, friend? We'd be grateful. Though, to head into the Thousand Maws, I'd say you'll need to gather a party of at some [@IF($E5(2,0),[@IF($E2(2,10),[@SWITCH(2,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(2)])],[@VALUE(2)])] to [@IF($E5(4,0),[@IF($E2(4,10),[@SWITCH(4,one,two,three,four,five,six,seven,eight,nine,ten)],[@VALUE(4)])],[@VALUE(4)])] companions.

'Course, you'd best make sure they actually entered the Maws before you go in after them. The guards stationed at the dungeon entrance will know.

[@SPLIT([@STRING($EB(1))], ,1)], is it? We had word from Nuala you would be coming. You mean to find the Ul'dahns who came ahead of you, yes?
Neither I nor Nuala granted them leave to enter the Maws. After I refused their demands, they sunk so low as to attempt a bribe, but Gridanian honor cannot be bought─least of all with Ul'dahn gil.

The Maws are a labyrinth of twisting tunnels and shafts, and break the surface in more places than one. Our eyes cannot be everywhere at once. It is possible they found another way in. It would not be the first time, nor the last, I venture.
There is even talk of moogles leading folk to secret entrances, though what possesses the furry little bastards is a mystery to me.

Whatever came of the Ul'dahns, I can't bloody well say if they are even in the Maws. You seem confident that they are. It might be you are privy to some knowledge I am not. But I don't much care in any event. You'll have to brave the Maws yourself if you wish to search for them.
The beasts within are in a frenzy the likes of which we've never seen in the Twelveswood. I will not refuse you entry, but I must insist on certain conditions.
Once you set foot in the Maws, I cannot permit you to re-enter until your body has had time to rid itself of the noxious residues of woodsin and aether which permeate the place.

After completing an expedition in the Thousand Maws of Toto[@1F]Rak, you will not be allowed to return immediately to the dungeon. To confirm how long you must wait before re-entering, view the Timers tab located under Attributes in the [@COLOR(#ff00cc22)][@EDGECOLOR(#ff262626)]main menu[@COLOR($EC)][@EDGECOLOR($EC)].

As another measure to prevent the untimely loss of life to the beasts lurking below, I shall be performing a special incantation prepared by the Conjurers' Guild to draw you and your party out of the dungeon after a set amount of time has passed.
You can remain in the Thousand Maws of Toto[@1F]Rak for a maximum of [@VALUE($E8(2))] minutes (Earth time) per visit.
In addition to my spell, you may leave at any time by returning to the entrance on foot.

There are also rumors of an imperial magitek device located in the farthest reaches of the dungeon. It is said the infernal machine can instantly return a man to this spot, but I am not sure I would trust anything constructed by the Empire. Who knows what sort of havoc the contraption might play on one's humours.

Finally, if you find yourself knocked unconscious by one of the creatures, our scouts have confirmed that using a Return spell will transport you back to the dungeon's entrance, so you may continue your mission, if you so wish.

That is all I can tell you for now. The truth is that we, too, are not fully apprised of the situation─including the role of the moogles in all this. We will provide you with what support we can, but you'd be wise not to let your guard down once inside.
Go and make what preparations you must. Speak to me again when you wish to enter.
